summary: Add enforceable quality-gate automation around the existing desktop and Streamlit reader changes, with security/dependency checks, measured coverage, independent review validation and auditable evidence.
requirement: User request: Mandatory Quality Gates for AI-Generated Code; includes the pending reader search, citation filtering and audio-prefetch work.
rationale: Preserve unittest and Node's existing runner; add coverage.py, c8 and deterministic Playwright integration checks. Use a separate trusted controller because PR code and artifacts are untrusted. Policy thresholds come from measured app coverage rather than arbitrary percentages.
assumptions: The owner designated McLeodolf for peer, architecture and security review. Additional independent reviewers are still needed for owner-authored and high-risk changes. The owner must confirm the Streamlit deployment branch. GitHub Actions is available for this public repository; no approval is inferred from designation.
compatibility: Desktop entry points, reading positions, DOM identifiers and the Streamlit requirements.txt deployment path are retained. Python dependency manifests are now hash-locked. Node dependencies are pinned. Windows GUI tests need a desktop-capable runner.

dependencies.name: Python runtime and build lockfiles
dependencies.reason: Resolve existing ranges to reproducible transitive versions with hashes.
dependencies.risk: Newly resolved versions and existing copyleft dependencies need independent dependency/license review.

dependencies.name: coverage, Bandit, pip-audit, Ruff, mypy
dependencies.reason: Measure behavior and implement security, dependency, lint and strict gate-core type checks.
dependencies.risk: Pinned CI tools run only in unprivileged jobs; advisory outages block results.

dependencies.name: Gitleaks and Semgrep CE engine
dependencies.reason: Detect secrets and Python/JavaScript security patterns, including negative fixtures.
dependencies.risk: Archives are checksum-pinned; native engine licensing/bundled libraries need explicit review. The vulnerable Semgrep Python MCP dependency is not installed.

dependencies.name: Vite 8.0.16
dependencies.reason: Patch vulnerabilities found in the prior 8.0.13 development server.
dependencies.risk: Verify generated frontend bundle consistency and browser behavior.

dependencies.name: c8, ESLint security plugins, Istanbul coverage adapters and Playwright
dependencies.reason: Collect line/branch and browser integration evidence using the existing frontend test stack.
dependencies.risk: Development dependencies only; mock external speech in CI to avoid paid or rate-limited requests.

verification: Use python -m quality.run and the trusted CI controller. Actual results are written to test-output/quality-current and CI artifacts; the readiness report records executed checks. Governance fixtures exercise both acceptance and expected failure without claiming real human approvals.
operations: No new runtime environment variables or database migration. CI uses only scoped GITHUB_TOKEN; the privileged controller executes protected code and reads candidate evidence as data. Complete independent reviewer onboarding and approve the baseline before activating branch protection. Feature-branch commit and push are explicitly authorized.
rollback: Revert the framework through a reviewed feature PR while retaining the current required check until a replacement has passed. Restore the previous application bundle and locked dependencies through the same gate. Do not disable checks or downgrade the baseline to clear a failure.
limitations: Local validation is not hosted enforcement. Publishing this feature branch does not install trusted controls on the default/target branches or activate branch protection. McLeodolf is designated but cannot approve his own PR; high-risk changes require two independent reviewers. Baseline approval and package/license reviews remain pending. Scanners do not prove the absence of malicious packages or application-level authorization defects.
threat_and_failure_analysis: Trust boundaries include EPUB archives/HTML, browser message traffic, speech service requests, cache files, external registries, untrusted PR code and CI artifacts. Preserve sanitization and resource bounds; test hostile EPUB input and cache reuse. Reject stale revisions, skipped/empty tests, altered workflow templates, unreviewed dependency changes, absent evidence, unauthorized reviews and expired exceptions. Controller failures remain blocked. Native GitHub Actions check identity cannot isolate a malicious repository administrator; stronger organizational controls or a separate GitHub App are required for that threat.
